claims.claim: Tens of comparisons change the leader in every design: 62 Arena votes, 92 expert and 143 GPT-4 judgments, 7 and 16 NBA games (drop, top-1).
Flip top-1 sizes are 46 (Arena), 46 (MT-Bench expert), 61 (GPT-4 judge), 4 and 8 (NBA 2014/2015).
Top-k set sizes: Arena top-5 21, MT-Bench expert top-3 229, GPT-4 judge top-3 150, NBA 2014 and 2015 top-5 1 game each.
Arena drop top-1 needs 0.046% of 135,622 votes; flip top-1 0.034%.
MT-Bench expert drop top-1 fraction 2.74%, flip 1.37%.
MT-Bench GPT-4 judge drop top-1 fraction 5.96%, flip 2.54%.
NBA season-mean top-1 fractions are 0.876% (drop) and 0.457% (flip); per-season drop fractions 0.531% and 1.22%.
Row counts n derived as k divided by the reported fraction: Arena 135,622; MT-Bench expert 3,355; GPT-4 judge 2,400; NBA 2014 1,319 and NBA 2015 1,311 (2x2 system).
Influence-ordered sets are about 15.7x smaller than random perturbations: mean clipped log2 ratio 3.975, 95% CI [3.934, 4.0], censored at the clip of 4.
Sizes coincide with the one-step influence comparator: mean log2 ratio 0.0, CI [0.0, 0.0]; equal top-1 drop fractions.
The pre-declared superiority test over the influence ordering is not supported.

Direct heuristic family scores are 0 for Arena, GPT-4 judge and NBA, and -0.0053 for MT-Bench experts; under the harness's stated (uninspectable) scoring rule the heuristic was marginally smaller in at least one MT-Bench-expert case.
The planted synthetic control returns k=8 with control score 0, which under the harness's stated score definition equals its enumerated minimum.
The row-permutation control returns 62, identical to the Arena drop top-1 size (score 0).
All 15 real-case sizes are identical across seeds 101, 102 and 103; replay match 1.0; failed-episode fraction 0.0.
The sealed evaluation completed with a qualified outcome (no failed episodes, replay matched); no per-gate diagnostics are recorded.
Drop-to-flip ratios for top-1 are 1.35, 2.0, 2.34, 1.75 and 2.0; flipping is always cheaper.
For MT-Bench the GPT-4 leader needs more drops for top-1 (143 vs 92; 5.96% vs 2.74%) but fewer for top-3 (150 vs 229; 6.25% vs 6.83%).
Fragility ordering of drop top-1 cases reverses between count (NBA 7, 16 before Arena 62) and fraction (Arena 0.0457% first).
Recorded episode time per seed over all 17 cases was 15.99 s, 15.55 s and 16.33 s.

The evaluated configuration is the baseline influence ordering; the three refined search configurations were all unscored (0 of 3 scored), the cause is not recorded, and their effect is unknown, not a loss.
Exact search and lower-bound certificates for minimal drop sets are computationally demanding beyond a few dimensions even for least squares, so heuristic sets are upper bounds.
Ranking recovery under BTL-type models with a fraction of adversarially corrupted comparisons is the setting the flip perturbation instantiates.
BT models are used for sports tournaments; we fit a static BT per NBA season.
